target_customer: Small Indian merchants and kirana shopkeepers who sell on informal credit
problem: Small merchants track credit given to customers on paper, which is slow to reconcile and makes collection hard.
business_model: Free ledger app, later premium subscription tiers plus payments and fintech services
product_category: Digital ledger and bookkeeping app for SMBs

founders.name: Harsh Pokharna
founders.background_notes: Named CEO by KrAsia (Oct 2019). Education and employers not stated in opened sources.

founders.name: Aditya Prasad
founders.background_notes: Named CTO by KrAsia (Oct 2019). KrAsia calls the three founders engineering graduates without naming a school.

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile ledger with reminders and offline sync is standard app engineering; scale across low-end Android phones and many languages was the main challenge.

defensibility.rationale: Merchants' ledger history creates some lock-in, but the feature set was easy to copy, and several rival ledger apps competed for the same merchants by 2019.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Payment players and rival ledger apps entered the space by 2019 per Inc42; OkCredit was not acquired and reported layoffs in early 2022 as it refocused.

market_need_then: The founders' YC description says over 50 million Indian SMBs issue informal credit, with a large share of sales on credit and records kept on paper. KrAsia reports the founders felt the pain themselves buying groceries on credit in 2017.

branding.domain_note: Uses okcredit.in rather than a .com; no acquisition story found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positions itself as a digital bahi khata, using the traditional ledger term in Hindi marketing.

brand_strength.rationale: Company claims over 1 crore downloads and use in 2,800+ cities on its own site, but no independent press on the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: OkCredit raised a 15.5 million dollar Series A and a 67 million dollar Series B within three months in 2019 on fast merchant adoption of a free ledger app. Rivals such as Khatabook and payment apps competed hard for the same merchants, and reports in early 2022 described layoffs of roughly 30 to 40 staff as it cut burn and refocused on fintech. It is still operating.
notes: No competitor source dated at or before the Summer 2018 batch was found; Khatabook coverage found is from Sept to Oct 2019 and Instamojo Credit Book from Nov 2019, so they are excluded from the as-of-founding list. A search snippet mentioned a 1.7 million dollar pre-Series A tied to YC, seen only in one snippet, unverified.
